newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish bond yields end lower, crown firmer.
newsitem.headline: Swedish bond yields end lower, crown firmer.

text.p: 1000 GMT - Swedish bond yields ended lower on Wednesday, supported by stronger international markets, and the crown firmed somewhat.
The market closed at 1000 GMT ahead of the Labour Day holiday on Thursday when markets will be closed.
Investors will eye Finance Minister Erik Asbrink's Labour Day speech to see whether he will voice an opinion about Swedish membership in Europe's economic and monetary union.
* Six-month T-bill rate slips one basis point to 4.29 pct
* Ten-year bond yield drops six basis points to 7.25 pct
* Crown firms to 4.5270 to mark vs 4.5340 late on Monday.
Swedish bond yields ended lower on Wednesday, supported by stronger international markets, and the crown firmed somewhat.
"The U.S. market remained strong after we closed on Tuesday and European yields have fallen, too," one trader said.
The market closed at 1000 GMT ahead of the Labour Day holiday on Thursday when markets will be closed.
"Trade has been quiet, as usual before a holiday," one dealer said.
The six-month T-bill rate slipped one basis point to 4.29 percent and the ten-year bond yield fell six to 7.25 percent.
The crown firmed somewhat to 4.5270 crowns to the mark versus 4.5340 crowns on Tuesday.
Investors will eye Finance Minister Erik Asbrink's Labour Day speech, half expecting him to to say whether he supports Swedish membership in Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU).
The government has not voiced its opinion on EMU and polls show that Swedes are fairly hostile to the idea of joining from the start in 1999.
